title: Count subarrays with given sum
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Count the number of subarrays whose sum equals K (negatives allowed).
intuition: sum(i..j) = pre[j] - pre[i-1] = K means pre[i-1] = pre[j] - K. So at each j add the *count* of earlier prefixes equal to pre[j] - K. Counting, not longest, so store frequencies.

approaches.title: Brute: all subarrays
Optimal: prefix-sum counts
approaches.idea: Seed the map with {0: 1} so prefixes that equal K on their own are counted.
approaches.code:
from collections import defaultdict


def count_subarrays_sum_k(a: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    freq = defaultdict(int)
    freq[0] = 1
    pre = 0
    count = 0
    for x in a:
        pre += x
        count += freq[pre - k]
        freq[pre] += 1
    return count

approaches.whyWorks: Every subarray corresponds to exactly one (start prefix, end prefix) pair.

edgeCases: K = 0 with zeros in the array
